# Layout

Layout helpers arrange dashboard components in rows or columns and add space between them. JavaScript helpers return DOM elements; Python helpers return serializable `View` objects.

<template v-if="language === 'js'">

## vconcat

`vconcat(...elements)`

Vertically concatenate components in a column layout.

## hconcat

`hconcat(...elements)`

Horizontally concatenate components in a row layout.

## vspace

`vspace(size)`

Vertical space to place between components. Number values indicate screen pixels. String values may use CSS units (em, pt, px, etc).

## hspace

`hspace(size)`

Horizontal space to place between components. Number values indicate screen pixels. String values may use CSS units (em, pt, px, etc).


</template>

<template v-else-if="language === 'python'">

## vconcat

`vg.vconcat(*items, param_names=None, **kwargs)`

Vertically concatenate components in a column layout.

## hconcat

`vg.hconcat(*items, param_names=None, **kwargs)`

Horizontally concatenate components in a row layout.

## vspace

`vg.vspace(value)`

Vertical space to place between components. Number values indicate screen pixels. String values may use CSS units (em, pt, px, etc).

## hspace

`vg.hspace(value)`

Horizontal space to place between components. Number values indicate screen pixels. String values may use CSS units (em, pt, px, etc).

## Children and spacing

JavaScript concatenation flattens child arrays by one level and appends the existing DOM nodes in order. Python concatenation keeps its arguments in order without flattening lists. Declarative `hconcat` and `vconcat` contain arrays of recursively nested components.

Numbers specify pixels. Strings can specify a [CSS dimension](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/dimension). The JavaScript runtime also converts numeric strings to pixels and defaults an omitted or undefined size to 10 pixels. Python requires a size argument. Spacer values are literal values; reactive parameters belong in the nested plot or input components.

## Python context

Python concatenation helpers accept `param_names` and the existing `View` keyword context, including `data`, `plot_defaults` and `config`. `View.to_dict()` and `vg.spec(...)` preserve caller-local parameter and data discovery. Plot directives keep their last supplied value. A layout preserves child order and shares the enclosing specification's parameters and plot defaults with its nested plots.

## Nested layout starters

Each starter creates nested layouts over a three-row SQL table. The concat starters combine both orientations and spacer axes. All starters bind a named radius parameter and use plot defaults for the nested charts. JSON/YAML declare a specification, JavaScript returns DOM, and Python serializes a `Spec`.
